rendering.persona_description: Sipho is a 52-year-old facilities manager for a mid-sized school district, transitioned in his late thirties, and has worked in the same district long enough that most colleagues just know him as Sipho. He coaches a rec-league softball team on weekends, which he loves, but skips the post-game bar gatherings almost every time. He's methodical about his tools and his truck, keeps a tidy toolbox and a tidier spreadsheet of work orders, and describes himself as someone who'd rather fix a boiler than make small talk about it.
rendering.clinical_context: Sipho has social anxiety centered on being watched or judged in group settings, especially meetings where he has to speak up, and situations where his voice or mannerisms might draw attention. It's been present since adolescence but got sharper after he transitioned, when he became newly self-conscious about being read or scrutinized in ways he wasn't before. He's currently in exposure-based treatment, doing graded exposure homework such as speaking up unprompted in staff meetings and staying at the post-game gatherings for a set amount of time before allowing himself to leave.
rendering.behavioral_description: Sipho is plainspoken and a little gruff, describing his week in concrete terms rather than feelings language, and he'll often downplay how hard an exposure was until pressed. He pushes back when something sounds like it's asking him to overshare or perform enthusiasm he doesn't feel, and he'll say so directly rather than going quiet about it. He tracks his own exposure homework like a work log and gets irritated when a suggestion seems to skip past what he's already tried.
